Thanks again for the call today, Alex & Priya  appreciate the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Summary of wants (from the call)
- Region routing: route US traffic to our us-central model pool, EU to eu-central (GDPR-bound data will always stay in EU pool).
- Latency vs cost policy: prefer p95 < 250ms for UI snippets; background batch reranks can tolerate 1s and use cheaper quantized variants.
- Fallback chain: primary: rtx-high (low-latency), fallback: rtx-cost (quantized) then hosted small model for best-effort.
- Structured output & tool calling: customer will use structured JSON responses for their triage UI, and want tool-calling for external knowledge-base lookup.
- Embeddings/reranker: use embeddings for semantic search (open-source embedder we provide) + a light cross-encoder reranker for top-10.

Attachments I pulled together: architecture diagram + SDK quickstart + a draft policy YAML. See attached: nexa-model-routing-arch.png, redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf, model-routing-policy-template.yaml.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):

2) Well share a sample model-routing policy YAML (attached) and a Dev-runbook for SDK install.
3) Proof-of-concept: we can onboard a single endpoint for the search UI using the routing + embedding pipeline for a 2-week POC.
4) Procurement: Alex, loop in procurement when youre ready and well send the contract summary.

Alex  great questions, answered inline below.

1) Region guarantees: Yes  for PHI-bound requests we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated per agreement. For hosted routing we can ensure model inference occurs in the requested region; minimal telemetry (request metadata hashed) may transit our control plane unless you opt for Private. Ive noted this as a must for scope if you want absolute isolation.

2) Fallback chain schema preservation: well enforce a structured-output contract at the route level. The routing policy will include a "response_contract" block that validates the JSON schema before returning to the caller; if the fallback returns a schema mismatch well either retry the next fallback or return a 202 with an error object depending on your preference. Ive attached a sample policy YAML that includes the response_contract snippet.

3) Embedding throughput: For a ~30M doc index we'd recommend sharded embedding workers + S3-backed vector store; throughput estimate: 200-800 qps aggregated depending on vector size and vector store selection. For the POC we can recommend a single-shard setup (50-100 qps) and scale to sharded service for production. Marcus  can you confirm the sizing numbers are in line with our infra benchmarks?

Proposed call times: Fri 20 Feb 2026 09:00-09:45 PST or Mon 23 Feb 2026 14:00-14:45 PST. What works?

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa / team  quick technical readout and proposed changes to the draft policy. See inline notes below and attached updated YAML (I exported as model-routing-policy-template.yaml).

- Region enforcement: For hosted we will enforce region execution by mapping X-Region to a region-specific model pool. Control-plane telemetry will be anonymized and routed through our regional control relays; for PHI we recommend Dedicated/Private as Marissa suggested.

- Response contract: Implement strict JSON schema validation at the gateway layer. If a fallback returns mismatched schema, we will automatically retry the next fallback once; if still mismatched return a 202 with an error payload that includes a schema_error field. This preserves a predictable public contract.

- Latency SLOs: Well attach p95 sampling and an opt-in for early-exit if latency exceeds threshold (i.e., return partial tokens with a status flag). For UI routes well set routing policy to prefer low-latency model variants and enable KV prefix cache where applicable.

- Fallback behaviour: primary -> secondary retry (once) -> tertiary best-effort. All fallbacks must conform to the response_contract before being accepted. We will instrument fallback metrics (fallback_rate, schema_mismatch_count).

- Embeddings sizing: For 30M docs we recommend 8 shards for production (approx 4M docs/shard) using approximate nearest neighbor index (HNSW) with incremental re-sharding plan. Throughput estimate: 600-900 qps aggregate with SSD-backed index and optimized batch sizes; initial POC: 2 shards (100-200 qps) to reduce cost/risk.

Next actions Ill take this afternoon:
- Update the policy YAML with response_contract and retry strategy.
- Draft SDK header examples (HMAC + short-lived API key rotation) and add to the runbook.
- Prepare a short demo snippet showing region routing header (X-Region) and a sample request/response preserving JSON schema.

Ill attach the updated YAML to the calendar invite for the Fri 09:00 PST sync.
